paragraphs: CyberNut sells phishing simulation training and email threat response to K-12 school districts, for staff and for students. It presents itself as a cheaper, education-first option next to the enterprise awareness vendors it names.

Districts run simulated phishing campaigns from a library of K-12 templates or their own, aimed at chosen groups, with difficulty adjusting on its own. Someone who clicks is assigned a short lesson automatically. Training runs as 30-second gamified lessons with rewards, leaderboards and progress tracking. When a message is flagged, the Active Threat Manager finds and removes it before it spreads. A learning centre covers NIST and DIR standards in short lessons.

The company claims more than 500 school districts nationwide. It says every simulation, lesson and report is made for how schools actually work rather than carried over from corporate training. A banner announces the acquisition of Neptune Navigate. The stated aim is to bring student digital citizenship and staff security awareness onto one platform.

quote.text: The moment a phishing email is reported, CyberNut deletes it from every inbox in the district.
